A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Conjuring Semantic Similarity. All 15 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original semantic-similarity evaluations, ablations, and word-level error analyses using diffusion models, including Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–3, together with the qualitative visualizations in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 are identical: both define semantic distance through diffusion-path Jeffreys divergence and compute it using Monte Carlo sampling.

E1.justification: Both versions use STS12–16, STS-B, SICK-R, RG65, and SimLex-999. The word-clustering examples and qualitative prompt scenarios, including Appendix A, are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same embedding, encoder, and autoregressive comparators, plus initial/final timestep prediction, direct output comparison, and the KL variant. Table 2 retains the same text-encoder Paragon comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain identical splits, sample counts, Spearman evaluation, model configurations, and ablation procedures. The default LMS scheduler, guidance scale 7.5, and T = 10 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The timestep-prior, Monte Carlo sample-count, diffusion-model, and denoising-step ablations are unchanged. Both versions retain the same part-of-speech error analysis, clustering analysis, and Appendix A case studies.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical average-and-spread reporting. Section 4.4 retains k = 1–5 and the reported ±0.77 variation across those choices; no seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match across Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–5. For example, Table 1 retains the proposed method's STS-B score of 70.3 and average of 65.4 ± 5.3.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same SDE definitions, regularity and Novikov assumptions, Girsanov-based KL derivation, and symmetrized distance construction. No mathematical argument is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 5 retain identical claims about imagery-grounded semantic similarity, visual interpretability, and evaluating diffusion models' semantic alignment with humans.

C2.justification: The interpretations of semantic transfer and word-level errors remain identical. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning abstract meanings, the text-encoder bottleneck, linguistic ambiguity, and computational cost.

D1.justification: Implementation and dataset details remain identical, including latent dimensions, RTX 4090 hardware, and approximately 2 seconds per Monte Carlo step. The new funding acknowledgement adds no technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and complete bibliography are unchanged. Reference entries move between pages following the acknowledgement insertion, without changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 adds Section 6, Acknowledgements, stating 'Research supported by ONR N00014-19-1-2229.' The first-page arXiv version/date marker also changes; all other prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement block shifts the References heading downward on page 10 and moves reference entries across pages 10–13. All five figures, three tables, and appendix layouts remain visually identical.

improvement.justification: v4 adds funding attribution in Section 6, updates the version/date marker, and adjusts reference layout. This supplies a small transparency benefit, but the scientific arguments, evidence, reproducibility details, limitations, and substantive presentation remain identical, yielding no meaningful overall quality change.
